outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no proof or counterexample of the universal inequality γ(G□H) ≥ γ(G)γ(H) has been posted in any source located, and the 2025–2026 preprints themselves describe it as open. The window instead holds partial results on its constant: a single-author density reframing with conditional or restricted results for bipartite graphs (Hosking, first posted 26 Aug 2025); a universal constant of about 0.5643 (Steiner, 12 Jun 2026); and the same arXiv identifier carrying a withdrawn constant of 0.5809 (1 Jul 2026, withdrawn 2 Jul 2026 for an 'algebraic mistake') and then a claimed universal constant of 2/3 (version 3, 9 Sep 2026), whose AI disclosure credits 'Claude (Fable 5)' with computational assistance on Theorems 1.1 and 1.4.
problem_asks: One universal claim, for every pair of graphs G and H: γ(G□H) ≥ γ(G)γ(H), where γ is the domination number and □ the Cartesian product. Parts: (1) the inequality with coefficient exactly 1; (2) for all pairs G and H, with no restriction on size, connectivity, or class. The statement asks for no constant other than 1, no approximate form, and no equality cases. Wikipedia's wording is only 'a relation between the domination number and the cartesian product of graphs' (lead, fetched); the inequality above is the standard form it names.

events.what_happened: Barcalkin and German (1979) proved the inequality with coefficient 1 for a class of graphs. Wikipedia attributes to them the case of graphs with domination number two; search snippets describe a 'partitioning condition' class (BG-graphs). The original paper was not read, and the two secondary descriptions differ.
events.delivers: Coefficient-1 inequality for a restricted class of graphs G (per secondary sources only), with H arbitrary.
events.remains: Every G outside that class, so the general inequality for all pairs.
events.time_since_posted: not assessed (1979)
events.doubts: The two secondary descriptions of the class disagree (domination number two in the Wikipedia article; a partitioning condition in search snippets). The original was not read.
events.direction: Full inequality on a restricted class; cuts toward the conjecture.

events.what_happened: W. Edwin Clark and Stephen Suen, 'An Inequality Related to Vizing's Conjecture', Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 7 (2000) #N4, DOI 10.37236/1542. Proves γ(G)γ(H) ≤ 2γ(G□H) for all simple graphs G and H. This is the baseline general bound every later source cites.
events.delivers: Universal bound γ(G□H) ≥ ½γ(G)γ(H) for all G and H. This is a weaker form (coefficient ½, not 1) and gives the inequality with coefficient 1 for no pair beyond trivial cases.
events.remains: The inequality with coefficient 1 for all G and H.
events.time_since_posted: not assessed (published 2000; the standard baseline bound)
events.direction: Partial, toward the conjecture (weaker constant).

events.what_happened: Elliot Krop, 'A brief, simple proof of Vizing's conjecture', arXiv:1109.0707. Version 1 (4 Sep 2011) abstract: 'In this note, we prove the conjecture', stated for general graphs. Version 2 (16 Sep 2011) is marked withdrawn, with the comment 'This paper has been withdrawn by the author due to a problem with the "label exchange"'. No journal version was found. The 2011 date is the arXiv date, not the 2013 date that one search snippet gave.
events.revisions: v2 16 Sep 2011, withdrawn by the author; text of v2 not available on the abstract page
events.delivers: As claimed: the full inequality γ(G□H) ≥ γ(G)γ(H) for all graphs. The claim was withdrawn, so as of this record it establishes nothing.
events.remains: The whole statement, if the withdrawal stands.
events.time_since_posted: about 15 years; no public engagement located, and no later paper located treats it as a proof
events.doubts: Withdrawn by its author for a 'label exchange' problem. The error is not described in any source located. The abstract claims a complete proof, not a special class.

withdrawn.what: v1 claimed a full proof; v2 withdrawn by the author with the comment 'This paper has been withdrawn by the author due to a problem with the "label exchange"'

events.direction: Claims to prove the conjecture in full; the claim was withdrawn.

events.what_happened: Stephen Suen and Jennifer Tarr, 'An Improved Inequality Related to Vizing's Conjecture', Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 19(1) (2012) P8. Per a search snippet, the improved bound is γ(G□H) ≥ ½γ(G)γ(H) + ½min{γ(G),γ(H)}. The fetched abstract restates only the ½ bound and does not state the min term, so the formula is unverified against the PDF.
events.delivers: Per the search snippet only: universal bound with a min term, weaker than coefficient 1 and slightly stronger than Clark–Suen.
events.remains: Coefficient 1 for all G and H.
events.time_since_posted: not assessed
events.doubts: The stated bound differs between the search snippet (min term) and the fetched abstract (½ only). The PDF was not read.
events.direction: Partial, toward the conjecture (weaker constant).

events.what_happened: Aziz Contractor and Elliot Krop, 'Vizing's Conjecture for Almost All Pairs of Graphs', arXiv:1502.00708 (v1, 3 Feb 2015). Abstract: if |G| ≥ γ(G)γ(H) and |H| ≥ γ(G)γ(H), then γ(G□H) ≥ γ(G)γ(H); a random-graph corollary follows for almost all pairs in a size range. The arXiv abstract page lists only v1. A search snippet claimed a March 2024 revision, which the page does not show.
events.revisions: Only v1 listed on the abstract page
events.delivers: The inequality with coefficient 1 for pairs in which both graphs have at least γ(G)γ(H) vertices, plus a random-graph consequence.
events.remains: Pairs in which either graph has fewer than γ(G)γ(H) vertices.
events.time_since_posted: about 11 years; no journal version found and no public engagement located
events.direction: Full inequality on a size-restricted class of pairs; partial, toward the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Boštjan Brešar, 'Vizing's Conjecture for Graphs with Domination Number 3 – a New Proof', Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 22(3) (2015) P3.38, DOI 10.37236/5182. Proves γ(G□H) ≥ 3γ(H) for any graph G with γ(G)=3 and any graph H, so the inequality holds whenever one factor has domination number 3. A search snippet says the γ ≤ 3 case was already known (L. Sun, 2004); that is unverified, and the note gives a new proof.
events.delivers: The inequality with coefficient 1 whenever one factor has domination number 3 (the other factor arbitrary). A restricted class.
events.remains: Pairs in which neither factor has domination number 3.
events.time_since_posted: not assessed
events.direction: Full inequality on the class of pairs with a factor of domination number 3; cuts toward the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Aziz Contractor and Elliot Krop, 'A class of graphs approaching Vizing's conjecture', arXiv:1512.01077 (v1, 3 Dec 2015; v2, 4 Apr 2016). Abstract: for any G in class A1, γ(G□H) ≥ (γ(G) − √γ(G))·γ(H). The arXiv comment gives Theory and Applications of Graphs 3(1) art. 4 (2016) as the venue.
events.delivers: A bound with coefficient γ(G) − √γ(G), which is below γ(G) for every G, so it is not the full inequality even on class A1.
events.remains: The full coefficient on class A1, and every G outside A1.
events.time_since_posted: about 10 years
events.direction: Partial, weaker than the conjectured coefficient on its class; toward the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Elliot Krop, 'Vizing's conjecture: a two-thirds bound for claw-free graphs', arXiv:1607.06936 (v1, 23 Jul 2016; v2, 29 Jun 2017), Discrete Applied Mathematics 230 (2017) 162–165, DOI 10.1016/j.dam.2017.06.017. Proves γ(G□H) ≥ (2/3)γ(G)γ(H) for claw-free G and any H.
events.delivers: Coefficient 2/3 (not 1) for claw-free G and any H. Weaker than the conjecture even on that class.
events.remains: Coefficient 1 on claw-free G, and every non-claw-free G.
events.time_since_posted: not assessed
events.direction: Partial, weaker coefficient on a class; toward the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Elliot Krop and Kimber Wolff, 'A new bound for Vizing's conjecture', arXiv:1608.02107 (v1, 6 Aug 2016; v2, 5 Sep 2025; 14 pages). Abstract: γ(G□H) ≥ π(G)/(2π(G)−1) · γ(G)γ(H), where π(G) is the 'power' of G (the minimum, over minimum dominating sets D, of the largest number of D-vertices in one closed neighbourhood). v1 abstract: with γ(G) in place of π(G), coefficient γ(G)/(2γ(G)−1); coefficient 2/3 for claw-free or P4-free G. v2 (text read): Thm 2.5 gives parity-split bounds; Cor 2.7 says Vizing's inequality holds when γ(G)=3. The change made in the 2025 revision is not identified.
events.revisions: v2 5 Sep 2025; the content change is not identified
events.delivers: For all G and H, coefficient π(G)/(2π(G)−1). This equals 1 exactly when π(G)=1, so the inequality holds in full for every G with π(G)=1. Otherwise the coefficient is below 1. v2 also gives the γ(G)=3 case.
events.remains: Graphs G with π(G) ≥ 2 and γ(G) ≠ 3, and any other pair the coefficient does not cover.
events.time_since_posted: about 10 years for v1; v2 posted Sep 2025 with no uptake located
events.direction: Partial. Full inequality for π(G)=1 and for γ(G)=3 in the v2 text; coefficient below 1 otherwise; toward the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Elliot Krop, Pritul Patel and Gaspar Porta, 'Vizing-type bounds for graphs with induced subgraph restrictions', arXiv:1705.04954 (v1, 14 May 2017). The abstract states that several Vizing-type bounds are proved for G with forbidden induced subgraphs. The fetch summary of the page says the coefficient-1 inequality is proved for G claw-free and P6-free, or K4- and P5-free, with other classes getting c < 1. The full text was not read.
events.delivers: Per the fetch summary only: the coefficient-1 inequality for G in two named hereditary classes (claw-free and P6-free; K4- and P5-free), with H arbitrary.
events.remains: Every other class of G, and the general case.
events.time_since_posted: about 9 years; no public engagement located
events.doubts: Scope rests on a fetch summary of the abstract, not the full text.
events.direction: Full inequality on restricted classes of G; toward the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Shira Zerbib, 'An improved bound in Vizing's conjecture', arXiv:1706.03682 (v1, 12 Jun 2017; v3, 25 Oct 2017). Abstract: γ(G□H) ≥ ½γ(G)γ(H) + ½max{γ(G),γ(H)}. No journal version was found in the opened sources.
events.delivers: Universal bound with coefficient ½ and a max term. For γ(G)=γ(H)=k > 1 it is strictly below γ(G)γ(H); it equals γ(G)γ(H) only when one factor has domination number 1.
events.remains: Coefficient 1 for all pairs except those where one factor has domination number 1.
events.time_since_posted: about 9 years
events.direction: Partial, weaker constant; toward the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Elisabeth Gaar, Daniel Krenn, Susan Margulies and Angelika Wiegele, 'An Optimization-Based Sum-of-Squares Approach to Vizing's Conjecture', arXiv:1901.10288 (v1, 29 Jan 2019); ISSAC '19 (Beijing, 15–18 July 2019), DOI 10.1145/3326229.3326239. Recasts the conjecture as a Positivstellensatz existence question, solves semidefinite programs for numeric sum-of-squares certificates, and converts them to exact symbolic certificates for particular graph classes. This is computer algebra, not AI.
events.delivers: The inequality with coefficient 1 for the graph classes for which certificates were found. No general proof.
events.remains: The general case, and every class without a certificate.
events.time_since_posted: not assessed

machine_checked.system: Semidefinite programming with sum-of-squares certificates converted to exact symbolic form by computer algebra (not a proof assistant)

events.directly_checkable: The certificates are polynomial identities that can be checked by computer algebra; the 2020 follow-up was not read.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture for the certified classes. No counterexample sought.
events.object: Sum-of-squares (Positivstellensatz) certificates showing that the Vizing polynomial is nonnegative on particular classes of graphs, found by semidefinite programming and converted to exact symbolic form. They certify finitely many classes and do not decide the universal statement. Explicit certificates are in the paper and its 2020 follow-up (not read).

events.what_happened: Gaar, Krenn, Margulies and Wiegele, 'Towards a computational proof of Vizing's conjecture using semidefinite programming and sums-of-squares', arXiv:2003.04021 (2020). A search snippet says it groups graphs by vertex count and domination number and gives exact, low-degree, sparse sum-of-squares certificates for particular classes; a later journal version (J. Symbolic Computation 107, 2021) is mentioned in a search snippet. Not opened.
events.delivers: Per a search snippet only: certificates for particular graph classes.
events.remains: The general case.
events.time_since_posted: not assessed
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture for the certified classes, per the snippet; not verified.

events.what_happened: Kimber Wolff, 'An improvement in the two-packing bound related to Vizing's conjecture', Theory and Applications of Graphs 7(1) (2020), DOI 10.20429/tag.2020.070105. Per a search snippet, it applies Zerbib's technique to Brešar's packing bound, giving a bound on γ(G□H) in terms of γ(G) and the 2-packing number of the other factor. Not opened; the exact formula is unverified.
events.delivers: Per a search snippet only: a partial universal bound involving the 2-packing number.
events.remains: Coefficient 1 for all pairs.
events.time_since_posted: not assessed
events.direction: Partial, toward the conjecture (weaker form); not verified.

events.what_happened: Boštjan Brešar, Mark Hartnell, Michael Henning, Hanna Kuenzel and Douglas Rall, 'A New Framework to Approach Vizing's Conjecture', Discussiones Mathematicae Graph Theory 41(3) (2021) 749–762, DOI 10.7151/dmgt.2293. Per the abstract as seen in search (not opened): combines the class-restricted route with the Clark–Suen partition, and gives γ(X□Y) ≥ max{½γ(X)γt(Y), ½γt(X)γ(Y)}, where γt is the total domination number.
events.delivers: Per the search abstract only: a Clark–Suen-type bound with coefficient ½ using total domination numbers; partial.
events.remains: Coefficient 1 for all pairs.
events.time_since_posted: not assessed
events.direction: Partial, weaker coefficient; toward the conjecture. Not verified beyond the search abstract.

events.what_happened: Elisabeth Gaar and Melanie Siebenhofer, 'Sum-of-Squares Certificates for Vizing's Conjecture via Determining Gröbner Bases', arXiv:2112.04007 (v1, 7 Dec 2021; v2, 11 Dec 2021; v3, 21 Jun 2023), Journal of Symbolic Computation (DOI 10.1016/j.jsc.2023.102236; volume 120 (2024) per a search snippet). Abstract: derives the unique reduced Gröbner basis of the Vizing ideal for the case where both domination numbers are 1, and from it the minimum degree of an SOS certificate, (nG+nH−1)/2. Also a method for graph classes using smaller semidefinite programs.
events.revisions: v2 11 Dec 2021; v3 21 Jun 2023; journal version 2023 online, volume 120 (2024) per a search snippet
events.delivers: Computer-algebra structure of the certificates: a Gröbner basis and the minimum certificate degree for the case where both domination numbers are 1 (where the inequality is trivially true, since any nonempty graph has γ ≥ 1). Certificates for graph classes are a computational result, not a general proof.
events.remains: The inequality for every pair with a domination number above 1, and the general case.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper (per the journal DOI)

events.time_since_posted: not assessed

machine_checked.system: Computer algebra (Gröbner bases) and semidefinite programming, implemented in SageMath (per a search snippet)

events.directly_checkable: The Gröbner basis and certificate degree are checkable by computer algebra; not checked here.
events.direction: Computational structure of certificates; does not move the inequality for any new pair. Toward the conjecture only in the sense of its certificate method.
events.object: Gröbner basis of the Vizing ideal in the γ=1 case, and the minimum-degree SOS certificate it implies. These are algebraic facts about the certificate method, not new instances of the inequality.

events.what_happened: Simon Špacapan, 'A note on Vizing's conjecture', arXiv:2212.09571 (v1, 19 Dec 2022). Proves a special case: if minimum dominating sets D1 and D2 of G exist such that, for every vertex h of H, the projection of D ∩ G_h onto G lies in D1 or in D2, then any dominating set D of G□H satisfies |D| ≥ γ(G)γ(H). No journal reference found.
events.delivers: The inequality with coefficient 1, under a projection hypothesis on minimum dominating sets of G. A conditional special case.
events.remains: Pairs for which no such pair of dominating sets exists, and the general case.
events.time_since_posted: about 4 years; no journal version found and no public engagement located
events.direction: Conditional special case of the inequality; toward the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Omar Tout, 'On the domination number of the cartesian product of the path graph and any pair of graphs', arXiv:2312.09208 (v1, 14 Dec 2023; v2, 30 Dec 2023). Abstract: γ(X□Y□P2) ≥ (2/3)γ(X)γ(Y) for any graphs X and Y. Improves Clark–Suen's ½ for products with an extra P2 factor. Not a result about the two-factor product.
events.delivers: Coefficient 2/3 for the product with a P2 factor added, where the right-hand side is γ(X)γ(Y) (not γ(X□Y)). This is a different question (three factors, one of them P2).
events.remains: The two-factor inequality γ(G□H) ≥ γ(G)γ(H) for all pairs; this is not the question the paper answers.
events.time_since_posted: about 2 years; no public engagement located
events.direction: A different question (product with an extra P2 factor). Partial, weaker coefficient for that question; does not bear on the two-factor coefficient 1.

events.what_happened: Omar Tout, 'Domination number of Cartesian product through space projections', Discrete Mathematics Letters 13 (2024) 95–99, DOI 10.47443/dml.2024.034, published online 11 July 2024 (per search results). Per search summaries: a lower bound on γ(X□Y□Z) using projections in space, and a derivation of the Clark–Suen bound from it. The PDF returned binary and was not readable, so the scope and the bound are from search summaries only.
events.delivers: Per search summaries only: a lower bound for a three-factor Cartesian product, which implies Clark–Suen's ½ bound as a special case. A different question (three factors).
events.remains: The two-factor inequality for all pairs; the paper does not address it.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (online 11 July 2024, per search results)

events.time_since_posted: about 2 years 3 months; no further engagement located
events.doubts: The PDF could not be read; the scope is from search summaries.
events.direction: A different question (three-factor products). Does not change what the two-factor entry asks.

events.what_happened: Noah Hosking, arXiv:2509.10473 (single author; no journal version found). Version 1 (26 Aug 2025) is titled 'Vizing's Conjecture: A Density-Based Re-framing'; later pages carry 'Domination Density and an Imbalance Regime for Vizings Conjecture'. The paper restates the conjecture as ρ(G□H) ≥ ρ(G)ρ(H) with ρ = γ/|V|, which is the original inequality divided by |V(G)||V(H)|. For bipartite G it gives a conditional sufficient condition: if a minimum dominating set of G is concentrated on one side of the bipartition relative to δ(H), then γ(G□H) + τ_X|V(H)| ≥ γ(G)γ(H), with τ_X depending on local domination concentration; it also shows that domination-reducing leaf deletions preserve the inequality. The v1 abstract additionally claims that the regular high-degree instance certifies 'all k-regular pairs for k ≥ 32' via the Arnautov–Payan bound. The v4 abstract (fetched) contains no regular-graph claim; the v5 abstract-page fetch reports the k ≥ 32 sentence, so this is unresolved.
events.revisions: v1 26 Aug 2025; v2 16 Sep 2025; v3 25 Oct 2025; v4 28 Feb 2026; v5 23 Aug 2026 (dates from the arXiv abstract page). Titles differ across versions. Search snippets report that v3 claimed a k ≥ 7 conditional regular result, which was not verified.
events.delivers: Bipartite pairs under an imbalance or concentration condition, giving an additive-deficit form of the inequality (for bipartite G with δ(G) > δ(H), per the abstract); the v1 claim covers all k-regular pairs for k ≥ 32 (v1 only, status in later versions unresolved). Restricted classes only.
events.remains: Non-bipartite G and H; bipartite pairs without the concentration condition; the general inequality. The leaf-deletion stability question is left open by the author.
events.time_since_posted: about 14 months as of 13 Oct 2026; no public engagement located in the sources opened
events.doubts: (1) The claimed scope changed across versions: the k ≥ 32 regular claim is in the v1 abstract, is absent from the v4 abstract, and is reported again in a v5 abstract-page fetch (unresolved). (2) By the author's own account (v5 full text, per fetch summary), the additive bound is weaker than the Clark–Suen bound and is meant to isolate a structural regime. (3) Single author, no journal publication located. (4) The density reframing is an algebraic restatement, so its content lies in the bounds.
events.direction: Partial, restricted regimes only, toward the conjecture. Does not establish the general inequality. Its additive bound is weaker than Clark–Suen's, by the author's own account.

events.what_happened: Raphael Steiner, 'A constant-factor step towards Vizing's conjecture', arXiv:2606.14414 (single version, v1, 12 Jun 2026; 10 pages). Theorem 1.3: for all graphs G and H, γ(G□H) ≥ c·γ(G)γ(H) with c = (5+√73)/24 ≈ 0.5643, the first constant-factor improvement of Clark–Suen's ½. The proof combines a new bound (Theorem 1.4, from an upper bound on γ_G(S) by induction and cell counting), Brešar's packing bound and a bound from Hou and Lu, then a case analysis over four ratio variables showing the maximum of the resulting expressions is at least c. Presented as a hand proof; no computer verification is claimed. AI disclosure (verbatim from the fetched HTML): 'We used ChatGPT 5.5 Pro to assist us with the search for literature surrounding Vizing's conjecture' and 'We also used it to help us check this document for misprints and typos.' This is not load-bearing mathematics, so no entry is recorded in ai.systems.
events.delivers: Universal inequality with coefficient c ≈ 0.5643 for all G and H. A weaker form (constant below 1); gives no pair with coefficient 1 beyond the trivial ones.
events.remains: Coefficient 1 for all G and H, the conjectured inequality.
events.time_since_posted: about 4 months as of 13 Oct 2026; no public check located. The later Aliabadi–Krop v3 abstract cites it and uses its constant as the prior best.
events.direction: Partial: a universal weaker constant; cuts toward the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Mohsen Aliabadi and Elliot Krop, 'An improved constant for Vizing's conjecture', arXiv:2607.01109, version 1 (1 Jul 2026). Abstract: γ(G□H) ≥ .5809·γ(G)γ(H). Version 2 (2 Jul 2026) is marked 'This paper has been withdrawn by Elliot Krop' with the comment 'Algebraic mistake'. The full text of v1 (HTML) contains no AI, LLM, or software-assistance statement.
events.revisions: v2 2 Jul 2026 (withdrawn); v3 9 Sep 2026 (retitled 'A 2/3 Bound for Vizing's Conjecture'; the claimed constant changed; see the separate event)
events.delivers: Universal inequality with constant .5809, as claimed. Weaker form (constant below 1). Withdrawn.
events.remains: Coefficient 1 for all G and H.
events.time_since_posted: about 3.5 months; withdrawn two days after posting; no check located
events.doubts: Withdrawn by its author with the comment 'Algebraic mistake'. The mistake is not described in any source located.

withdrawn.what: v1 claim γ(G□H) ≥ .5809 γ(G)γ(H) withdrawn by the author; v2 marked withdrawn with the comment 'Algebraic mistake'

events.direction: Partial: universal constant .5809, weaker than the conjectured coefficient 1. Withdrawn.

events.what_happened: Mohsen Aliabadi and Elliot Krop, arXiv:2607.01109, version 3 (9 Sep 2026; comment 'We fixed the argument and made an improvement. 10 pages'), retitled 'A 2/3 Bound for Vizing's Conjecture'. Abstract (fetched HTML): for all finite graphs G and H, γ(G□H) ≥ (2/3)γ(G)γ(H), 'raising the best known universal constant in the approximate form of Vizing's conjecture' from Steiner's (5+√73)/24 to 2/3. Theorem 1.1: for a 2-packing P of H with r = |P|, W = V(H) ∖ N_H[P] and s = γ_H(W), γ(G□H) ≥ rγ(G)/3 + (r+s)(2γ(G) − ρ(G))/3, where ρ(G) is the 2-packing number of G. Theorem 1.3 (the 2/3 bound) follows by applying Theorem 1.1 to a maximum 2-packing of H (Corollary 1.2, inequality (7)) and dropping a nonnegative absolute-value term, per the fetched text. The fetched text says no computer search, finite check or linear program is used for Theorem 1.3; Section 6 (Proposition 6.1) is a hand-checked linear-programming-style analysis. Theorem 1.4 is a second bound in the same setting. AI disclosure (verbatim from the fetched HTML): 'During the preparation of this work, the authors used Claude (Fable 5) for language editing, to improve the clarity and readability of the manuscript, and for computational assistance related to the proofs of Theorems 1.1 and 1.4.' The next sentence says: 'The authors subsequently reviewed, verified, and edited all AI-assisted content as needed'. The disclosure does not say what the computational assistance produced.
events.revisions: v1 1 Jul 2026 (constant .5809, separate event); v2 2 Jul 2026 (withdrawn); v3 9 Sep 2026 (this event). The 2/3 mathematics first appears in v3.
events.delivers: As claimed: universal inequality with coefficient 2/3 for all G and H. Weaker form (coefficient below 1); claims to beat Steiner's constant.
events.remains: Coefficient 1 for all G and H, and the gap between 2/3 and 1.
events.time_since_posted: about 5 weeks as of 13 Oct 2026; no public engagement located
events.doubts: (1) The same authors' previous version was withdrawn two months earlier for an 'algebraic mistake', and it claimed a different constant; the v3 comment says 'We fixed the argument', and the text does not describe what changed. (2) Theorem 1.3 rests on Theorem 1.1, and the AI disclosure names Theorem 1.1 among the proofs that received 'computational assistance' without saying what that assistance produced. (3) The step from Steiner's 0.5643 to 2/3 came about three months after Steiner's v1, and no independent check is located. These are recorded as signals, not verdicts.
events.direction: Partial: universal inequality with coefficient 2/3; weaker than the conjectured coefficient 1. Claims to improve the best known universal constant.

systems.name: Claude (Fable 5)

The authors state that they 'reviewed, verified, and edited all AI-assisted content as needed'. What the computational assistance produced (a computation, a check, a proof step, or code) is not stated.

disputes.summary: Sources differ on the conjecture's date: 1968 (Brešar et al. survey, Wikipedia) against 1963 (some search snippets and an older thesis). This is an attribution question about the conjecture, not a priority dispute over a result.

summary: Forty-four web searches and more than two dozen page fetches (arXiv abstract and HTML pages for about twenty identifiers, the Electronic Journal of Combinatorics pages for four papers, and the Wikipedia article). No source located reports a proof, disproof or counterexample of the universal inequality since 26 January 2024. The Wikipedia lead (fetched) lists the problem as open, and cites no 2024–2026 result. The 2025–2026 preprints themselves say the conjecture is open. Four in-window events concern a weaker form, a constant below 1, rather than the coefficient-1 statement. (i) Hosking, arXiv:2509.10473, first posted 26 Aug 2025: a single-author density reframing with conditional or restricted results for bipartite graphs, revised through v5 (23 Aug 2026). (ii) Steiner, arXiv:2606.14414, 12 Jun 2026: a hand proof of γ(G□H) ≥ 0.5643·γ(G)γ(H) for all graphs. Its AI disclosure says the author used 'ChatGPT 5.5 Pro' for literature search and a typo check. That is not load-bearing, so ai.systems is empty and none_found is false. (iii) Aliabadi and Krop, arXiv:2607.01109 version 1, 1 Jul 2026: a claimed constant of .5809, withdrawn in version 2 on 2 Jul 2026 with the comment 'Algebraic mistake'. (iv) The same identifier's version 3, 9 Sep 2026, retitled 'A 2/3 Bound for Vizing's Conjecture', claiming γ(G□H) ≥ (2/3)γ(G)γ(H) for all finite graphs. Its AI disclosure credits 'Claude (Fable 5)' with language editing and 'computational assistance related to the proofs of Theorems 1.1 and 1.4'. The fetched text says Theorem 1.3 follows from Theorem 1.1 by a short inequality and that no computer step is described for Theorem 1.3. So the AI-assisted part is the partition theorem on which the 2/3 bound depends. The disclosure does not say what the computational help produced; this is the record's central unresolved AI question. Tout's Discrete Mathematics Letters paper (online 11 July 2024, PDF not readable) is an in-window item, but per search summaries it concerns three-factor products, a different question. Pre-window history is recorded as events with predates_frozen_revision true: Barcalkin and German (1979, restricted class); Clark and Suen (2000, the ½ baseline, checked on the EJC page); Krop's 2011 claimed full proof, withdrawn by its author on 16 Sep 2011 for a 'label exchange' problem; Contractor and Krop (2015, size-restricted pairs, and class A1 with γ − √γ); Brešar (2015, the γ = 3 case, checked on the EJC page); Krop (2016, claw-free 2/3, DAM 2017); Krop and Wolff (2016, a π-parameter bound that equals 1 when π(G) = 1, and the γ = 3 corollary in the 2025 v2); Krop, Patel and Porta (2017, coefficient 1 on some restricted classes, per a fetch summary); Zerbib (2017, ½γγ + ½max, checked on the abstract page); Gaar et al. (2019 and 2020) and Gaar and Siebenhofer (2021), which use computer algebra and semidefinite programming on graph classes and are not AI; Špacapan (2022, a conditional special case); Tout (2023, a P2 factor, a different question); and Suen–Tarr (2012), Wolff (2020) and the 2021 DMGT paper, which are search-only. Close calls: (a) the 2025–2026 papers treat the universal constant as the approximate form of the question. The statement names coefficient 1, so on a strict reading every constant result is a weaker form and settles nothing. (b) Hosking's k ≥ 32 regular claim is in the v1 abstract and in the latest abstract-page fetch, but not in the v4 abstract or the v5 full text. This is unresolved. (c) The dates for Brešar (2015) and Tout (2024) are journal dates; no earlier preprint was found. (d) The quotations from 2607.01109 v3 and 2606.14414 v1 come from the fetch tool's extraction of the arXiv HTML. They should be checked against the PDFs. The AI search (about a dozen queries pairing the conjecture with AI, GPT, Claude, AlphaEvolve, FunSearch, Erdős problems and Lean) found no AI-credited proof or counterexample of this conjecture. The AI-credited results that surfaced in graph-domination searches (a GPT-5.6 eternal-domination disproof, a Teschner bondage-number counterexample, a GPT-5.6 cycle double cover claim) concern other problems and are not recorded as events.
competing_reading: The strongest case for a different reading: the coefficient in the statement is the quantity the conjecture asserts equals 1, and the best known universal constant is the nearest measurable proxy for it. On that reading the 2/3 claim (Aliabadi and Krop, v3) moves a named quantity from ½ to 2/3, Steiner's 0.5643 moves it from ½ to about 0.56, and the 2/3 result is the largest in-window movement. The AI step then sits inside the proof of a claimed movement. The opposing reading: the 2/3 proof is short and checkable by hand, since Theorem 1.3 is a one-line consequence of Theorem 1.1 per the fetched text, so the AI-assisted computation is not the source of the mathematics; but the same authors withdrew a constant two months earlier for an algebraic mistake, and no independent check is located. A third reading treats Hosking's regular-graph claim as a restricted case that moves nothing, which holds whichever version is current.
what_would_settle_it: For the 2/3 claim: a refereed publication, or a written check by a named combinatorialist of Theorem 1.1 and the deduction of Theorem 1.3, plus the authors' account of what 'computational assistance related to the proofs of Theorems 1.1 and 1.4' produced (a computation, a check, or a proof step). For Steiner's constant: an independent check of the four-variable case analysis. For Hosking: the status of the k ≥ 32 regular claim in the current version, and a check of the bipartite imbalance criterion. For the question as stated (coefficient 1 for all pairs): a proof or a counterexample that a named expert has checked.
